meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 您是东海经纪的涂盛涂总吗？我是荣思伦哥哥的铁杆大影迷，你能不能跟他说一声我要嫁给他！
examples.trans: Wait — are you Director Tu Sheng of Donghai Talent? I'm Rong Silun's biggest die-hard fan; please tell him I want to marry him!

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

examples.text: 一百人。
examples.trans: One hundred people.

examples.text: 一百个。
examples.trans: One hundred.

examples.text: 详细流程我们再过一遍，我觉得这个时间上可能有点问题。
examples.trans: Let's run through the detailed rundown one more time; I think the timing might be tight.

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān. Cardinal number 3; combines with measure words (三个) and floors (三楼).

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: 三瓶牛奶、二十个鸡蛋、黄油、奶酪和红苹果！
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān shí. Cardinal number thirty ('three tens'); pairs directly with measure words like 三十年 ('thirty years').

examples.text: 这棵老树在院子里长了三十年。
examples.trans: This old tree has grown in the courtyard for thirty years.

examples.text: 从客栈走到地铁站只要三十分钟。
examples.trans: Walking from the inn to the metro station takes only thirty minutes.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng. Used both as a directional verb/complement ('up, onto') and location word ('on top of').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià. Used for downward motion ('go down'), location ('under'), or 'next' (下周).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Friendly farewell xiàcì jiàn.

examples.text: 今天聊得很开心，下次见！
examples.trans: Great chatting today, see you next time!

examples.text: 我们下次见！
examples.trans: See you next time!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù. Standard negation for present/future/habitual verbs and adjectives; shifts to bú before a 4th tone (不是 bú shì).

examples.text: 停电的时候，纸还能用。
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhōng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个中心 ('a center').

examples.text: 我梦寐以求的咖啡馆，就开在自家庭院里！等着瞧我去告诉整条街的人吧！
examples.trans: My dream café—right in our own courtyard! Wait until I tell the whole street!

examples.text: 这是我人生中最棒的第一周！
examples.trans: This is the best first week of my whole life!

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Pinyin: èr. Used in counting, ordinals (第二), room numbers, and multi-digit numbers (二十); use 两 before measure words.

examples.text: 是的，宋老师，二楼四号房！坐火车累吗？
examples.trans: Yes, Teacher Song, room four on the second floor! Was the train ride tiring?

examples.text: 二十五年前我在附近教钢琴，不过记忆淡了。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano nearby, though memories fade.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liàng. Describes bright light or a surface polished clean (擦亮 'polish bright').

examples.text: 隔壁的小洗手间呢？灯亮吗？
examples.trans: What about the small bathroom next door? Does the light work?

examples.text: 火苗亮了——稳稳的蓝火，正合适。
examples.trans: The flame is lit—steady blue fire, right as it should be.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cóng. Marks a starting point in space or time (从早上到晚上 'from morning to night').

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wèi. Polite counterpart of 个 when counting guests, customers, or teachers (一位客人, 这位老师).

examples.text: 太谢谢你们两位了。
examples.trans: Thank you both so very much.

examples.text: 七点半有八位饿肚子的客人下楼啊！
examples.trans: At seven thirty, eight hungry guests are coming downstairs!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎ. Colloquial fusion of 两个, never followed by 个 (我们俩 'the two of us').

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

examples.text: 别动，你们俩。听到路边汽车停下的声音了吗？
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiōng dì. Measure word (量词): 对 (duì), e.g. 一对兄弟 ('a pair of brothers').

examples.text: 宋老师，快多讲讲梧桐巷那两兄弟吧！
examples.trans: Teacher Song, tell me more about those two brothers on Wutong Lane!

examples.text: 听听保养大师说的！昨天修热水器，今天修两兄弟！
examples.trans: Listen to the maintenance master! Yesterday fixing the boiler, today fixing two brothers!

related.gloss: a pair of brothers (measure word 对)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiān. Placed before the verb to sequence actions: 先…再… ('first…, then…').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Numeral bāshí ('eighty').

examples.text: 今天上午要完成八十分钟的拍摄素材。
examples.trans: This morning we need eighty minutes of usable footage.

examples.text: 这位年过八十的老歌唱家依然嗓音洪亮。
examples.trans: Past eighty, the veteran singer still has a ringing voice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liù. Cardinal number 6.

examples.text: 老陈……小晴……快告诉我今晚六号房空着。
examples.trans: Chen... Qing... please tell me room six is free tonight.

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: verb 关 plus resultative 上 emphasizing closing completely

examples.text: 我说的关门，是在外边把门关上。
examples.trans: When I said close the door, I meant close it from the outside.

examples.text: 外面太吵了，把窗户关上吧。
examples.trans: It is too noisy outside; let us close the window.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. Marks a next step in sequence (先提再推) or a future repetition (再见 'see you again').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: fēn zhōng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 五分钟 ('five minutes').

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: gāng. Placed right before a verb to show the action happened moments ago.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 一到七号钥匙全拿走了，八号房刚刷了油漆。
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is taken, and room eight just got fresh paint.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bié. Most commonly means 'do not' in polite commands (别担心 'don't worry'); as a verb, 'pin/clip on'.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 您先坐下，别着急，我们马上看行李牌。
examples.trans: Please sit down first and do not worry; we will check the luggage tag right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào. Works as main verb ('arrive') or result complement ('succeed in reaching/perceiving', 找到, 听到).

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qián. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个前面 ('a front side').

examples.text: 二十五年前我在附近教钢琴，不过记忆淡了。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano nearby, though memories fade.

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

examples.text: 那我也不能不管吧，这怎么办啊？
examples.trans: Well, I cannot just ignore it either — what should I do?

examples.text: 把这件事交给他去办，你完全可以放心。
examples.trans: Leave this matter to him to handle — you can rest completely assured.

meanings.en: by all means; be sure (not) to
meanings.note: Pinyin: qiān wàn. Strong, caring emphasis before 别 or 要 (千万别忘 'whatever you do, don't forget').

examples.text: 我还没喝早咖啡呢，千万别说急事！
examples.trans: I have not had my morning coffee yet; please do not say emergency!

examples.text: 小美，千万别因为我们多忙活。
examples.trans: Mei, please do not go to extra trouble on our account.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǐ. Read zhǐ as the adverb 'only' before verbs, and zhī as a measure word for cups, boxes, and small animals.

examples.text: 而且他今晚八点到这里——只剩四十分钟了！
examples.trans: And he arrives here at eight o'clock this evening—in forty minutes!

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hào. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个号码 ('a number').

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tīng. Focuses on the act of listening; add 见 or 到 (听见, 听到) for actually hearing.

examples.text: 老陈，你听到了吗？有人按了大门门铃！
examples.trans: Chen, did you hear that? Someone rang the front gate bell!

examples.text: 我在院子里老远就听到你们喊黄油了。
examples.trans: All the way out in the courtyard I heard you shouting about butter.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ne. After a noun, asks 'what about X?' (你呢？); at the end of a statement, highlights an ongoing situation.

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hé. Joins nouns or pronouns ('A and B'), NEVER two whole clauses; also means 'with' (和你一样).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.en: we; us; our (inclusive of both the speaker and the listener)
meanings.note: Pinyin: zánmen. Unlike 我们 (which can exclude the listener), 咱们 specifically includes the person spoken to, creating a warm, collegial, or colloquial tone. Directly modifies nouns without 的 in set expressions like 咱们这行.

examples.text: 干咱们这行，谁不想跟他学习？
examples.trans: In our line of work, who wouldn't want to learn from him?

examples.text: 淳于总已经批准咱们的方案了。
examples.trans: Director Chun Yu has already approved our proposal.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎng. Used for bells, phones, pipes, or alarms ringing or clanking.

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

meanings.note: Pinyin: la. Colloquial fusion of 了 + 啊 adding cheerful energy at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 你们守着，我出门啦！
examples.trans: Hold the fort—I am heading out the door!

meanings.note: Pinyin: huí. As a verb, 'return' (回家, 回来); as a measure word, 'occasion/time' (这回 'this time').

examples.text: 那个人为什么不拿回自己的箱子就跑了？
examples.trans: Why did that person run off without taking his own suitcase back?

examples.text: 他没要回那个装木头小火车的箱子吗？
examples.trans: Did he not ask back for that case with the wooden train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

场.gloss: measure word for rainstorms, shows, events

meanings.en: measure word for rainstorms, shows, events
meanings.note: Pinyin: chǎng. Counts bouts of rain or performances (一场大雨 'a heavy rainstorm').

examples.text: 我在做梦吗？！志豪，这场重逢是你安排的吗？
examples.trans: Am I dreaming?! Zhihao, did you plan this whole reunion?

examples.text: 昨晚下了一场大雨。
examples.trans: There was a heavy rainstorm last night.

meanings.en: sound; voice; measure word for sounds
meanings.note: Pinyin: shēng. Counts cries, knocks, or chimes (一声 'one sound').

examples.text: 来不及了！他说了声谢谢就挂断了！
examples.trans: Too late! He said thank you and hung up!

examples.text: 非常安静！不过刚才你听到奇怪的金属敲击声了吗？
examples.trans: Very quiet! Though did you hear a strange metallic knocking sound just now?

meanings.en: to prepare in advance; have ready for guests or use
meanings.note: Pinyin: bèi. Compact spoken and written verb often paired with 好 in 备好 ('all prepared and ready').

examples.text: 千万别碰它！一号桌已经备好热薄荷茶、红茶和温盘子啦。
examples.trans: Do not touch them! Table one already has hot mint tea, black tea, and warm plates ready.

examples.text: 小美提前备好了四碗洗净的夏莓和温蜂蜜糖釉。
examples.trans: Mei prepared four bowls of rinsed summer berries and warm honey glaze ahead of time.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià tiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个夏天 ('a summer').

examples.text: 房东律师寄来的？奇怪——我们房租一直交到明年夏天了。
examples.trans: Sent by the landlord's lawyer? Strange—our rent is paid right through next summer.

examples.text: 夏天坐在大树底下乘凉最舒服。
examples.trans: Sitting in the shade beneath the big tree in summer is bliss.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wài tou. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 外头院子 ('the space outside').

examples.text: 有人吗？晚上好！大门前根本没人啊！
examples.trans: Hello? Good evening! Nobody is standing at the gate!

examples.text: 周经理，看院子窗户外头——有人跑进大门了！
examples.trans: Manager Zhou, look out the courtyard window—someone just ran in the gate!

meanings.en: unexpected wonder; astonishing stroke of luck
meanings.note: Pinyin: qí jì. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè). Combines 奇 (extraordinary) with 迹 (trace, feat).

examples.text: 真是奇迹中的奇迹，周经理，眼镜稳稳架在您鼻梁上呢！
examples.trans: Miracle of miracles, Manager Zhou—your glasses are sitting squarely right on the bridge of your nose!

examples.text: 不到三个小时就把蛋糕和座位全赶出来，真算小院里的奇迹了。
examples.trans: Getting both the cakes and seating finished in under three hours was a real Courtyard Inn miracle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo. Main adjective 'good'; as a result complement after a verb, means 'ready/completed properly' (修好, 准备好).

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tā. Third-person singular pronoun for objects, animals, and places.

examples.text: 是啊，宋老师，还在等它的主人呢。
examples.trans: Yes, Teacher Song, still waiting for its owner.

examples.text: 别念叨它，宋老师！我现在差不多喜欢上那两声响了。
examples.trans: Don't tempt it, Teacher Song! I have almost grown fond of those two rings now.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kè rén. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位客人 ('a guest').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

meanings.en: sun hat woven from straw with a broad brim
meanings.note: Pinyin: kuān biān cǎo mào. Measure word (量词): 顶 (dǐng), e.g. 一顶宽边草帽 (a wide-brimmed straw hat).

examples.text: 走在志豪身边那位，拄着银手杖，戴着宽边草帽……
examples.trans: And walking beside Hao with a silver walking stick and a wide-brimmed straw hat...

examples.text: 五月太阳越来越晒，小美在院子摘薄荷时也戴上了宽边草帽。
examples.trans: As the May sun grew stronger, Mei also wore a wide-brimmed straw hat while picking mint in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo shí. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个小时 ('an hour').

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

examples.text: 七点整——比早餐早半个小时。
examples.trans: Seven sharp—half an hour earlier than breakfast.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo yuàn kè zhàn. Eight-room boutique courtyard inn on Wutong Lane in Chengdu.

examples.text: 欢迎来到小院客栈，小晴。明天不会无聊了。
examples.trans: Welcome to Courtyard Inn, Qing. Tomorrow will not be boring.

examples.text: 小院客栈，早上好！我是小晴。
examples.trans: Courtyard Inn, good morning! This is Qing speaking.

就位.gloss: take one's post, be in position

meanings.en: take one's post, be in position
meanings.note: Verb-object jiùwèi ('be in position on set').

examples.text: 助阵的同学们全部都已经就位了。
examples.trans: All the cheering classmates are in position.

examples.text: 四号机位已经就位了吗？
examples.trans: Is Camera Four in position yet?

meanings.note: Pinyin: chà. Tells minutes 'to' the hour (差五分十二点 'five to twelve') or 'not short a cent' (一分不差).

examples.text: 十、十一、十二。一分不差，谢谢！
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last cent—thank you!

examples.text: 十二点以后再拆吧，老板！看钟：差五分十二点！
examples.trans: Open it after twelve, boss! Look at the clock: five minutes to twelve!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǐ jīng. Often pairs with sentence-final 了 (已经到了 'has already arrived').

examples.text: 没错！你已经很习惯这儿了。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

examples.text: 还好烤箱里的面团已经放进去了。
examples.trans: My dough is already in the oven, at least.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì zhèng. Measure word (量词): 项, e.g. 一项市政 ('municipal service').

examples.text: 房产信？让志豪和我看看——我管市政合同，他懂老建筑保护法！
examples.trans: A property letter? Let Zhihao and me see it—I handle municipal contracts, and he knows heritage building law!

examples.text: 市政工人正在修路边的石板。
examples.trans: Municipal workers are repairing the flagstones along the road.

examples.text: 真的没事，再说了，我们刚好给布小谷开一个庆祝会！
examples.trans: Honestly it's fine — besides, we just used the time to throw Bu Xiaogu a promotion party!

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎng shàng. Directional phrase 往 ('toward') + 上 ('up'), placed directly before action verbs (往上抬 'lift upward').

examples.text: 先把窗板轻轻往上抬一点，再往外拉。
examples.trans: Lift the shutter slightly upward first, then pull outward.

examples.text: 到了中间部分，圆舞曲的旋律一步步往上升。
examples.trans: In the middle section, the waltz melody climbs upward step by step.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎng wài. Directional phrase 往 ('toward') + 外 ('outside').

examples.text: 透过擦干净的拱窗往外看，整个院子绿油油的。
examples.trans: Looking outward through the clean arched window, the whole courtyard is lush green.

examples.text: 这两扇木头窗板是往外推开的。
examples.trans: These two wooden shutters swing open outward.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wēi xiào. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个微笑 ('a smile').

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 哎呀！透过窗户看见周经理了？我明明加倍用力微笑了！
examples.trans: Oh dear! You spotted Manager Zhou through the window? I smiled twice as wide!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhì háo. Given name of Zhipeng's older brother, an acoustic architect.

examples.text: 没关系！您就是志豪先生吧？
examples.trans: No problem at all! You must be Mr Zhihao, right?

examples.text: 是的，我叫志豪。昨天打电话订了七号房。
examples.trans: Yes, my name is Zhihao. Yesterday I booked room seven by phone.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhì péng. Given name of Zhihao's younger brother.

examples.text: 白纸里面包的东西是给我哥哥志鹏的，不是我的。
examples.trans: What is wrapped inside that white paper is for my brother Zhipeng, not mine.

examples.text: 您为什么不直接去志鹏家门口把木头小火车交给他呢？
examples.trans: Why not go straight to Zhipeng's door and hand him the wooden train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: nín. Respectful singular 'you' used with elders, teachers, and guests (您好！).

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chéng. Frequently serves as a result complement meaning 'into' (变成, 改成).

examples.text: 商业办公楼出售？！把我们的客栈和厨房变成灰色办公室？！
examples.trans: Commercial office sale?! Turn our inn and kitchen into grey offices?!

examples.text: 超过八十年的小院建筑，只要一楼每天服务街坊邻居，禁止改成私人办公室。
examples.trans: Any courtyard building over eighty years old may not become private offices as long as the ground floor serves neighbours daily.

meanings.note: Pinyin: pinyin. This is a part used in conversational Mandarin.

examples.text: 我有一个我的。
examples.trans: I have a 我的.

examples.text: 这是一个非常好的我的。
examples.trans: This is a very good 我的.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dài. Specifically for accessories placed on the head, face, neck, or wrist—contrast 穿 for clothes/shoes.

examples.text: 哎呀，怎么拿错了！我戴眼镜看看行李牌。
examples.trans: Dear me, what a mix-up! Let me put on my glasses and check the luggage tag.

examples.text: 完了！昨天我没戴眼镜，在平板上接了电话预订！
examples.trans: Disaster! Yesterday without my glasses I took a phone booking on the tablet!

meanings.note: Pinyin: fáng. Measure word (量词): 间 (jiān), e.g. 一间房 ('a room').

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

扇.gloss: measure word for doors and windows

meanings.en: measure word for doors and windows
meanings.note: Pinyin: shàn. Counts hinged or sliding doors and windows (一扇门 'a door', 一扇窗户 'a window').

examples.text: 上楼梯，平台往左拐，最上面最后一扇门。
examples.trans: Up the stairs, turn left at the landing, last door at the very top.

examples.text: 再往左拐进小广场，找一扇蓝木门。
examples.trans: Then turn left into the small square and look for a blue wooden door.

meanings.en: walking stick; gentleman's or traveler's cane
meanings.note: Pinyin: shǒu zhàng. Measure word (量词): 根 (gēn) or 把 (bǎ). Combines 手 (hand) with 杖 (staff).

examples.text: 走在志豪身边那位，拄着银手杖，戴着宽边草帽……
examples.trans: And walking beside Hao with a silver walking stick and a wide-brimmed straw hat...

examples.text: 老地图师把手杖轻轻靠在八号房门边，笑着打量整座院子。
examples.trans: The retired mapmaker leaned his walking stick gently beside Room Eight's door and smiled at the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used in 扣工资 ('dock wages').

examples.text: 为了在会上替原创节目发声，她宁愿被扣一个月工资。
examples.trans: To speak up for original shows, she gladly let them dock a month's pay.

examples.text: 违反考勤制度的员工将会按规定被扣绩效分。
examples.trans: Staff who violate attendance rules have performance points deducted.

meanings.en: measure word for handled objects; disposal marker
meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎ. Counts items with handles or backs (一把钥匙, 一把椅子); as a preposition, fronts a definite object before an action verb.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎ shou. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个把手 ('a door/suitcase handle').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 旁边的把手上系着一张小纸牌。
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied on the side handle.

拄.gloss: to lean on (a cane or stick)

meanings.en: to walk leaning on a cane or staff
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǔ. Specific hand-radical verb paired almost exclusively with canes and sticks (拄手杖, 拄拐).

examples.text: 走在志豪身边那位，拄着银手杖，戴着宽边草帽……
examples.trans: And walking beside Hao with a silver walking stick and a wide-brimmed straw hat...

examples.text: 老教授虽然拄着银手杖，走起梧桐巷的石板路却精神得很。
examples.trans: Though leaning on a silver walking stick, the old professor stepped briskly along Wutong Lane's flagstones.

拎.gloss: to carry by a handle or strap

meanings.en: to lift and carry something dangling from one's hand (bag, basket, hatbox)
meanings.note: Pinyin: līn. Everyday verb contrasting with 抱 (hug in arms), 扛 (hoist on shoulder), and 捧 (cradle in both hands).

examples.text: 对呀，特别礼貌的两位徒步客——还有位拎花纹帽盒的文静女士订了六号房！
examples.trans: Yes, such polite hikers—and a quiet lady carrying a floral hatbox booked Room Six!

examples.text: 难不成徒步客把双肩包拎去六号房，而帽盒去了二号房？！
examples.trans: Don't tell me the hikers hauled their backpacks to Room Six while the hatbox went to Room Two?!

meanings.note: Pinyin: gǒng mén. Compound 拱 ('arch') + 门 ('door/gate'). Measure word: 道 (dào) or 扇 (shàn).

examples.text: 志豪在速写本上画下了院子的石头拱门。
examples.trans: Hao sketched the courtyard's stone archway in his sketchbook.

examples.text: 穿过这道砖拱门，就能看见后面的小花园。
examples.trans: Walk through this brick archway and you can see the little garden behind.

meanings.en: lift up; carry (by a handle); mention
meanings.note: Pinyin: tí. Used for lifting a door handle or carrying a bag by its strap/handle.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.en: to shake back and forth; ring a hanging or hand bell
meanings.note: Pinyin: yáo. Used for ringing gate bells (摇门铃), shaking bottles, or trees swaying.

examples.text: 三点出租车一到门口，记得把门铃摇两下！
examples.trans: As soon as your taxi pulls up at three, remember to ring the gate bell twice!

examples.text: 有人把黄铜门铃摇了两下——那是兄弟俩的暗号！
examples.trans: Someone just rang the brass gate bell twice—that is the signal from the brothers!

meanings.note: Pinyin: cā. Used for wiping tables, drying water, or polishing lanterns.

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

examples.text: 先生，给您干毛巾擦外套，还有一碗热汤。
examples.trans: Sir, here is a dry towel to wipe your coat, plus a bowl of hot soup.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qiāo. Used for knocking on doors or pipes clanking.

examples.text: 听……街口钟楼开始敲十二下了！
examples.trans: Listen... the clock tower at the end of the street is starting to strike twelve!

examples.text: 十二下敲完了……大门外面街上空荡荡的。
examples.trans: Twelve chimes have finished... and the street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhéng zhěng. Placed before numbers to stress entirety (整整六年 'six whole years').

examples.text: 何止认识！整整六年，每个星期五我都爬那座木楼梯教钢琴！
examples.trans: More than know it! Every Friday for six whole years I climbed those wooden stairs to teach piano!

examples.text: 这架老钢琴他已经弹了整整三十年。
examples.trans: He has played this old piano for a full thirty years.

meanings.note: Pinyin: páng. Compact locality noun placed after nouns (钢琴旁 'beside the piano', 窗旁 'by the window').

examples.text: 宋老师正坐在阳光房的钢琴旁微笑呢。
examples.trans: Teacher Song is sitting beside the piano in the sunroom smiling.

examples.text: 客栈大门旁挂着一块擦得发亮的铜牌。
examples.trans: Beside the inn's front gate hangs a brightly polished brass plaque.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù. Describes old houses, pipes, or letters—never a person's age (use 老 for people).

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个星期 ('a week').

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 脑子转得快，小晴。志豪每星期都读城市建筑规定。
examples.trans: Quick thinking, Qing. Hao reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Links two nouns (我是小晴); do NOT use simple 是 before plain adjectives like 好 or 忙.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì bú shì. A-not-A affirmative-negative question tag; bù shifts to bú before 4th-tone shì.

examples.text: 我们俩是不是刚升职当上正式试吃员了？
examples.trans: Did the two of us just get promoted to official taste testers?

examples.text: 你是不是把绿色登记本夹在胳膊底下了？
examples.trans: Didn't you tuck the green guest book under your arm?

meanings.note: Pinyin: àn. Describes dim lighting or a concealed door.

examples.text: 您尽管看，宋老师。星期一下午大堂暗。
examples.trans: Go right ahead, Teacher Song. Monday afternoon the lobby was dim.

examples.text: 走廊里的灯光有点暗。
examples.trans: The light in the hallway is a little dim.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǒu. Expresses both possession ('I have') and existence ('there is'); ALWAYS negated with 没 (没有), never 不.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

meanings.en: someone; somebody; there is someone who
meanings.note: Pronounced yǒurén; existential-indefinite expression introducing an unspecified person as the agent of the following verb, or indicating that a room/seat is occupied.

examples.text: 尹正宇来不了这边，当然是有人泄露了消息。
examples.trans: Yin Zhengyu cannot come to our side; obviously someone leaked the news.

examples.text: 要不是有人爆了照片，我估计两天都撑不住。
examples.trans: Had someone not leaked that photo, I reckon it would not have lasted two days.

meanings.note: Pinyin: péng you. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个朋友 ('a friend').

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 今天有两位老朋友从外地来看我。
examples.trans: Two old friends are visiting me from out of town today.

架.gloss: measure word for pianos, planes, framed machines

meanings.en: measure word for pianos, planes, framed machines
meanings.note: Pinyin: jià. Counts pianos, airplanes, and framed instruments (一架钢琴 'a piano').

examples.text: 三年前爷爷去世以后，我和志鹏因为卖老房子大吵了一架。
examples.trans: Three years ago after Grandfather passed away, Zhipeng and I argued bitterly over selling the old house.

examples.text: 客厅角落里放着一架老钢琴。
examples.trans: An old piano stands in the corner of the living room.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuō. Measure word (量词): 张 (zhāng), e.g. 一张桌子 ('a table').

examples.text: 等等——小美这会儿正要把蛋糕端到他们那桌去。
examples.trans: Wait—Mei is taking the cake out to their table right now.

examples.text: 从明天早上八点开始！屋里四张桌，树下三张桌！
examples.trans: Starting tomorrow morning at eight! Four tables indoors, three tables under the tree!

meanings.note: Pinyin: wú tóng xiàng. Tree-lined lane in Chengdu where Courtyard Inn stands.

examples.text: 等一下……梧桐巷十二号，角落里还写着两个童年名字的首字母！
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, Wutong Lane, with two childhood initials written in the corner!

examples.text: 宋老师，您一脸惊讶！您认识梧桐巷十二号吗？
examples.trans: Teacher Song, you look amazed! Do you know Number twelve, Wutong Lane?

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎn chá. Used for checking pipes, tags, or rooms.

examples.text: 我只是检查安全。这是我的工作。
examples.trans: I am simply checking security. That is my job.

examples.text: 谢谢您这么体谅！老陈马上去地下室检查。
examples.trans: Thank you for being so understanding! Chen will check the basement right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zōng sè. Measure word (量词): 种 (zhǒng), e.g. 一种棕色 ('a shade of brown').

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

examples.text: 等等——柜台上这本棕色小皮笔记本是谁的？
examples.trans: Wait—whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

related.gloss: a shade of brown (measure word 种)

meanings.note: Pinyin: huān yíng. Warm greeting to arriving guests (欢迎！ / 欢迎光临！).

examples.text: 大家早上好！欢迎你，小晴。都准备好了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Qing. Is everything ready?

examples.text: 欢迎光临！早上好，您好！
examples.trans: Welcome! Good morning, hello!

meanings.en: right in the middle of; squarely; right
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèng. Before a verb, marks an action in progress right now; before 对着, means 'directly/squarely'.

examples.text: 正合我心意。楼梯在哪儿？
examples.trans: Just what I wanted. Where are the stairs?

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

meanings.en: along; following the course of a road, river, or edge
meanings.note: Pinyin: yán. Often followed by 着 (zhe) to form 沿着 ('following along').

examples.text: 今天绝对不钻周经理那些小巷子——沿着梧桐巷直奔中央车站！
examples.trans: Definitely no diving into Zhou's little side alleys today—straight down Wutong Lane to Central Station!

examples.text: 两位客人沿着青石板小路慢慢走，一边走一边看灯笼。
examples.trans: The two guests walked slowly along the flagstone path, admiring the lanterns as they went.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wēn. Describes lukewarm water or mild temperatures.

examples.text: 摸摸热水管——下面是温的，上面变凉了。
examples.trans: Feel the hot-water pipe—the bottom is warm, while the top is turning cool.

examples.text: 壶里的水还是温的，正好喝。
examples.trans: The water in the pot is still warm—just right to drink.

meanings.note: Pinyin: diǎn. Marks hours on the clock (八点 'eight o'clock') or 'a bit' (一点).

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè. Describes hot tea, hot water, or warm weather.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: pí. Measure word (量词): 张 (zhāng), e.g. 一张皮 ('a piece of leather').

examples.text: 等等——柜台上这本棕色小皮笔记本是谁的？
examples.trans: Wait—whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

examples.text: 啊，我的皮笔记本！谢谢！我正到处找呢。
examples.trans: Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was looking everywhere for it.

related.gloss: a piece of leather (measure word 张)

meanings.note: Pinyin: pí xié. Measure word (量词): 双 (shuāng), e.g. 一双皮鞋 ('a pair of leather shoes').

examples.text: 怪不得这么重，全是木头和皮鞋！
examples.trans: No wonder it was so heavy—all wood and leather shoes!

examples.text: 下雨天出门，最好别穿新皮鞋。
examples.trans: Heading out in the rain, it is best not to wear new leather shoes.

related.gloss: a pair of leather shoes (measure word 双)

meanings.note: Pinyin: pán zi. Combines 盘 ('plate/tray') + nominal suffix 子 (zi); measure word: 个 (gè) or 只 (zhī).

examples.text: 干净盘子先放五分钟，你们俩快到门口来听！
examples.trans: Leave the clean plates for five minutes, both of you—come listen at the door!

examples.text: 小晴把烤好的柠檬挞切开，整整齐齐摆在白瓷盘子里。
examples.trans: Qing sliced the baked lemon tart and arranged it neatly on white porcelain plates.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhēn. Exclamatory adverb before adjectives (真好！ 'How nice!') or adjective 'genuine'.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

examples.text: 真奇怪！我们坐同一班早火车到同一个区。
examples.trans: How strange! We rode the very same morning train to the same district.

meanings.note: Emphatic adverb zhēnshi ('really is').

examples.text: 您真是厉害，写出这么好的稿子。
examples.trans: You are truly impressive to write such sharp pieces.

examples.text: 今天真是辛苦大家了。
examples.trans: Everyone truly worked hard today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mī. Action verb for narrowing the eyes into a slit to read small print or smile warmly (眯着眼睛看 'squint to read').

examples.text: 小晴把价钱写得很大很清楚，谁都不用眯着眼睛费力去看。
examples.trans: Qing wrote the prices big and clear so nobody has to squint to read them.

examples.text: 院子里的老猫晒着太阳，舒服得眯起了眼睛。
examples.trans: Basking in the sun in the courtyard, the old cat narrowed its eyes contentedly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǎn jìng. Measure word (量词): 副 (fù), e.g. 一副眼镜 ('a pair of glasses').

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 我的眼镜怎么会在……哎呀！在我头上！
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be in... oh dear! They are on my head!

related.gloss: a pair of glasses (measure word 副)

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhe. Placed right after a verb to show a state or posture continues (门开着 'the door stands open').

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

examples.text: 你瞧，窗台上的茉莉花今天早上全开了！
examples.trans: Look—the jasmine flowers on the windowsill all bloomed this morning!

examples.text: 快去瞧瞧，是谁把这包点心留在门廊的长椅上了？
examples.trans: Go take a quick look—who left this parcel of pastries on the porch bench?

meanings.note: Pinyin: pèng. Used for touching objects or running into someone (碰到 'bump into').

examples.text: 拐弯小心点，别碰到墙！
examples.trans: Careful on the turn—do not bump the wall!

examples.text: 我在街口正好碰到了老邻居。
examples.trans: I happened to run into an old neighbor at the corner.

meanings.note: In 磨破嘴皮子, means wearing out one's voice talking.

examples.text: 劝了他整整一个下午，嘴皮子都快磨破了。
examples.trans: Spending all afternoon persuading him nearly wore my voice out.

examples.text: 新皮鞋刚穿的时候有点磨脚。
examples.trans: Brand-new leather shoes chafe the feet a bit at first.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wén wěn. Reduplicated adverb describing steady hands or footing.

examples.text: 火苗亮了——稳稳的蓝火，正合适。
examples.trans: The flame is lit—steady blue fire, right as it should be.

examples.text: 她双手稳稳地端起盛满热茶的托盘。
examples.trans: With both hands she lifted the tray of hot tea steadily.

meanings.note: Verb/noun xiào ('smile, laugh').

examples.text: 你看着我的笔记笑什么？
examples.trans: Why are you smiling at my notes?

examples.text: 听到这个好消息，大家都开心地笑了。
examples.trans: Hearing the good news, everyone smiled happily.

meanings.note: Pinyin: děng deng. Urgent or casual reduplication of 等 ('wait!').

examples.text: 等等，深蓝色的，跟您的一样啊！
examples.trans: Wait—it is dark blue, the same as yours!

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiāng. Bound/free root of 箱子 ('chest/box/suitcase'), used in 木箱 ('wooden chest') and 工具箱 ('toolbox').

examples.text: 阁楼角落里放着一只带铜锁的旧木箱。
examples.trans: In the corner of the attic sits an old wooden chest with a brass lock.

examples.text: 这箱新鲜黄柠檬是今天早上刚从果园运来的。
examples.trans: This crate of fresh yellow lemons was brought straight from the orchard this morning.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hóng chá. Measure word (量词): 杯 (bēi), e.g. 一杯红茶 ('a cup of black tea').

examples.text: 宋老师早！您想喝咖啡还是红茶？
examples.trans: Morning, Teacher Song! Would you like coffee or black tea?

examples.text: 请给我不加糖的红茶，再来一片热面包。
examples.trans: Black tea without added sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.

related.gloss: a cup of black tea (measure word 杯)

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǎo. Describes longtime friends, historic lanes, or warm respect before a colleague's surname (老陈).

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 所以老房子自己会打招呼？
examples.trans: So the old house says hello by itself?

meanings.en: walnut wood; dark fine-grained timber used for pianos and frames
meanings.note: Pinyin: hú táo mù. Modifies furniture directly, e.g. 胡桃木钢琴 ('walnut piano').

examples.text: 快告诉我志豪躲哪儿去了——咱们得在那架胡桃木钢琴前实打实练够三十分钟！
examples.trans: Now tell me where Hao is hiding—we need thirty solid minutes at that walnut piano!

examples.text: 这张地图镶在温润的胡桃木画框里，挂在白墙上特别精神。
examples.trans: Set inside its warm walnut frame, the map looks striking hanging on the white lobby wall.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bò he chá. Measure word (量词): 壶, e.g. 一壶薄荷茶 ('a pot of mint tea').

examples.text: 宋老师，给您热薄荷茶和蜂蜜。
examples.trans: Teacher Song, here is hot mint tea and honey for you.

examples.text: 晚饭后喝一壶热薄荷茶最助眠了。
examples.trans: A pot of hot mint tea after dinner helps you sleep soundly.

related.gloss: a pot of mint tea (measure word 壶)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xī zhuāng. Combines 西 ('Western') + 装 ('attire/suit'); measure word: 套 (tào, full suit) or 件 (jiàn, suit jacket).

examples.text: 老陈笑着说：“您的老花镜安安全全装在西装口袋里呢，老板！”
examples.trans: Chen smiled and said, 'Your reading glasses are tucked safe and sound in your suit pocket, boss!'

examples.text: 为了迎接下午三点的审核，周经理特意穿上了一套整洁的深蓝西装。
examples.trans: To welcome the three-o'clock review, Manager Zhou put on a neat dark-blue suit.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jì de. Describes recalling something from memory.

examples.text: 钱箱里拿五十块，记得要收据！
examples.trans: Here is fifty yuan from the cash box; remember to get a receipt!

examples.text: 这么多年过去了，您还记得？
examples.trans: After all these years, you still remember that?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǒu. Means 'walk' (走路, 直走) or 'leave / head off' (我先走了).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Urgent conversational adverb gǎnjǐn.

examples.text: 赶紧告诉我。
examples.trans: Hurry up and tell me.

examples.text: 赶紧去休息吧。
examples.trans: Hurry and get some rest.

meanings.note: Compound shēnbiān ('beside one's body').

examples.text: 不要在我身边安插眼线。
examples.trans: Stop planting informants around me.

examples.text: 朋友都在身边。
examples.trans: Friends are all around me.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chē. Measure word (量词): 辆 (liàng), e.g. 一辆车 ('a vehicle').

examples.text: 送牛奶的车在城外坏了。你们看冰箱！
examples.trans: The milk delivery van broke down outside town. Look at the fridge!

examples.text: 门口停着一辆蓝色的出租车。
examples.trans: A blue taxi is parked outside the gate.

related.gloss: be stuck in a traffic jam

meanings.note: Pinyin: qīng qīng. Reduplication of 轻 ('light/soft'), used directly before short verbs or with 地 (轻轻地抽出来).

examples.text: 宋老师用两根手指把旧乐谱轻轻抽了出来。
examples.trans: Teacher Song gently slid the old music sheet out with two fingers.

examples.text: 怕吵醒午睡的客人，小晴轻轻关上了木门。
examples.trans: So as not to wake guests napping at noon, Qing closed the wooden door softly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà. Distal demonstrative before measure words (那个 'that one'); at clause start, means 'then / well then'.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 里面 ('the inside').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhōng lóu. Measure word (量词): 座 (zuò), e.g. 一座钟楼 ('a clock tower').

examples.text: 听……街口钟楼开始敲十二下了！
examples.trans: Listen... the clock tower at the end of the street is starting to strike twelve!

examples.text: 老广场北边的石钟楼每到整点都会敲钟。
examples.trans: The stone clock tower north of the plaza chimes every hour on the hour.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gāng qín. Measure word (量词): 架 (jià), e.g. 一架钢琴 ('a piano').

examples.text: 二十五年前我在附近教钢琴，不过记忆淡了。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano nearby, though memories fade.

examples.text: 何止认识！整整六年，每个星期五我都爬那座木楼梯教钢琴！
examples.trans: More than know it! Every Friday for six whole years I climbed those wooden stairs to teach piano!

meanings.note: Pinyin: tiě. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块铁 ('a piece of iron').

examples.text: 这把大铁扳手吗？给你。
examples.trans: This big iron wrench? Here you go.

examples.text: 一辆黄色出租车刚停在铁大门外头！
examples.trans: A yellow taxi just pulled up outside the iron gate!

related.gloss: a piece of iron (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: yín. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块银子 ('a piece of silver').

examples.text: 这是三楼阁楼门的小银钥匙。
examples.trans: Here is the small silver key to the third-floor attic door.

examples.text: 太松一口气了！志豪先生，给您银钥匙。
examples.trans: What a relief! Mr Zhihao, here is your silver key.

related.gloss: a piece of silver (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: mén. Measure word (量词): 扇 (shàn), e.g. 一扇门 ('a door').

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 这是三楼阁楼门的小银钥匙。
examples.trans: Here is the small silver key to the third-floor attic door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mén líng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个门铃 ('a doorbell').

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huáng tóng. Literally 黄 ('yellow/golden') + 铜 ('copper/bronze'): copper-zinc brass alloy.

examples.text: 钢琴琴槌里面的细小轴销是用结实的黄铜做的。
examples.trans: The tiny hinge pins inside piano hammers are made of sturdy brass.

examples.text: 老陈把前台的黄铜小铃铛擦得金光发亮。
examples.trans: Chen polished the little brass bell on the front desk until it gleamed.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bí liáng. Measure word: 根 (gēn) or 条 (tiáo); classic spot where glasses rest.

examples.text: 你跨出门槛之前，好歹先把老花镜架到鼻梁上呀！
examples.trans: At least put your reading glasses onto the bridge of your nose before you cross the threshold!

examples.text: 周经理笑着推了推鼻梁上的眼镜，细细念起成都老院文化节的来信。
examples.trans: Smiling, Manager Zhou nudged the glasses up the bridge of his nose and read the Historic Courtyard Festival letter aloud.
